S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S073.name: Distorted_Cognitions_With_Blame
S073.description: Persistent, distorted cognitions about the cause or consequences of the traumatic event that lead the individual to blame himself/herself or others.

subtypes.Self-Blame: Blaming oneself for the occurrence of the trauma or for not preventing it.
subtypes.Blaming Others: Distorting the situation to blame specific others for the occurrence or damage of the trauma.

S074.name: Persistent_Negative_Emotional_State
S074.description: Persistent negative emotional state (e.g., fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame).

subtypes.Persistent Fear: A state of constant fear, anxiety, and tension.
subtypes.Persistent Horror: The shock and terror of the traumatic moment do not fade and remain.
subtypes.Persistent Anger: A state of chronic anger boiling inside or being expressed aggressively.
subtypes.Persistent Guilt: Unceasing feelings of guilt or remorse related to the trauma.
subtypes.Persistent Shame: Continuing to feel shame or humiliation due to the trauma.

S075.name: Social_Detachment
S075.description: Feelings of detachment or estrangement from others.

subtypes.Emotional Detachment: Feeling cut off from others even when physically present, unable to feel connection.
subtypes.Social Isolation: Increasingly isolating oneself and not participating in social activities or gatherings.
subtypes.Difficulty with Intimacy: Distancing oneself from close people as it is difficult to become emotionally close.
subtypes.Loss of Belonging: Feeling like an outsider who belongs nowhere.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.

subtypes.Impulsive Anger: Sudden explosions of anger for trivial reasons or no clear reason.
subtypes.Verbal Aggression: Attacking others with shouting, cursing, or blame without holding back.
subtypes.Physical Aggression: Physically attacking people or throwing/breaking objects.
subtypes.Chronic Irritability: A state where nerves are always sharp and sensitive, ready to explode at the slightest touch.

S078.name: Reckless_Self_Destructive_Behavior
S078.description: Reckless or self-destructive behavior pattern that endangers one's safety or health.

subtypes.Risky Behaviors: Reckless actions disregarding consequences, such as speeding, dangerous sports, or criminal acts.
subtypes.Substance Abuse: Excessive drinking or drug use to harm oneself.
subtypes.Indisicriminate Sexual Behavior: Engaging in unprotected or dangerous sexual activities repetitively.
subtypes.Self-Harm: Actions that intentionally harm or scar one's own body.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.

subtypes.Scanning for Danger: Always scanning the surroundings and being alert to find potential threats or risks.
subtypes.Safety Checking: Repetitively confirming safety, such as checking exit locations or observing people around.
subtypes.Sustained Alertness: Unable to relax tension even in safe environments and maintaining a constant state of alertness.

info.persona: Heidi Barrera, a disciplined yet curious community champion, weaves together meticulous organization, boundless sociability, and a love for preserving local stories, even if they hoard discount coupons and occasionally lose their knitting needles.
info.professional_persona: Heidi Barrera, a retired community organizer and volunteer coordinator in Belvidere, leverages her humanities background, meticulous budgeting, and knack for rallying neighbors to design intergenerational mentorship programs, secure lasting grants for the town’s community garden, and lead the senior center with a blend of compassion and disciplined execution.
info.cultural_background: Heidi was raised in a Midwestern white family with deep roots in Illinois; her grandparents came from German and Irish immigrant backgrounds. Growing up in a small town near Belvidere, she absorbed values of community involvement, self‑reliance, and church participation, attending a Methodist congregation throughout her life. She earned a BA in humanities from a state university, which fostered a lifelong appreciation for literature, history, and cultural preservation, shaping her current dedication to local heritage and intergenerational goodwill.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Heidi enjoys reading historical fiction and biographies, researching family genealogy, tending to her vegetable garden, quilting and sewing, cooking meals for friends and community gatherings, attending local theater productions, leading walking tours of historic sites, and participating in senior fitness and book‑club meetings at the community center.
info.sports_persona: Heidi Barrera, a devoted fan of the Chicago Cubs and Chicago Bears who enjoys joining the senior bowling league at the local alley, incorporates weekly walking tours of historic Belvidere landmarks and participates in low-impact fitness classes at the community center, embracing an active lifestyle that balances nostalgia for classic Midwestern sports with gentle exercise.
info.arts_persona: Heidi Barrera, who regularly attends performances by the Belvidere Community Players and enjoys reading the works of Philippa Gregory, often knits while listening to folk legend Joan Baez, and finds inspiration in the paintings of local artist Susan Sherwood, letting the arts shape her communal storytelling pursuits.
info.travel_persona: Heidi Barrera, who has explored the historic streets of Philadelphia’s Old City, taken a road-trip through the Amish farms of Lancaster County, and dreams of a guided tour of the castles along Germany’s Rhine River, plans her journeys around senior travel discounts and the desire to connect local heritage with broader world histories.
info.culinary_persona: Heidi Barrera, an avid gardener and home-cook, frequently prepares roasted beet and carrot salads drizzled with honey-mustard vinaigrette, bakes classic apple crisp using heirloom apples from her orchard, and delights friends with her signature potluck lasagna layered with fresh mozzarella, all while occasionally over-salting her soups when lost in conversation.

info.persona: Lacedrick Williams is a gospel‑driven pastor‑in‑training who balances scholarly curiosity with street‑level hustle, impulsively upgrades camera gear, monitors asthma with tech, and channels community rhythm into every sermon and song.
info.professional_persona: Lacedrick Williams blends rigorous theological study with hands‑on ministry, delivering sermons that fuse gospel tradition and contemporary social‑justice insights while they coordinate youth programs, manage church communications, and apply their knack for organization and flexible problem‑solving.
info.cultural_background: Lacedrick is rooted in the African‑American tradition of the church, drawing from the rich legacy of Black spirituality, gospel music, and community activism. Raised in the Bronx, he has been shaped by a multicultural neighborhood that includes Caribbean, Latinx, and immigrant cultures, which informs his inclusive preaching style and his fluency in conversational Spanish. Family narratives of the Great Migration and civil‑rights struggles instill in him a sense of resilience and responsibility to uplift his community. He honors his heritage through participation in Black History Month events, supporting local Black artists, and integrating cultural symbols such as the African drum and spoken‑word poetry into worship.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside the pulpit, Lacedrick nurtures a love for literature, especially African‑American poetry and historical nonfiction. He spends evenings shooting street photography in the Bronx, capturing the vibrancy of community life. A regular on the neighborhood basketball court, he enjoys the camaraderie and physical release the game provides. Music is both a hobby and a ministry: he plays acoustic guitar, writes gospel‑inspired melodies, and curates playlists that blend classic soul with contemporary hip‑hop. He also volunteers at a community garden, experimenting with healthy soul‑food recipes.
info.sports_persona: Lacedrick Williams courts regular games at the Bronx Community Center's 5‑on‑5 pickup league, follows the New York Knicks and New York Yankees with fervor, and supports New York City FC during the soccer season, balancing competitive play with a relaxed jogging routine when the weather allows.
info.arts_persona: Lacedrick Williams curates a personal playlist featuring gospel legend Kirk Franklin, soulful pianist Alicia Keys, and socially conscious rapper Kendrick Lamar, writes acoustic hymns inspired by poetry that celebrates resilience and community of their neighborhood's church traditions, and attends local open‑mic nights where spoken‑word performances echo rhythmic storytelling reminiscent of Jacob Lawrence’s visual narratives.
info.travel_persona: Lacedrick Williams prefers budget‑friendly trips that blend cultural immersion and community service, having explored New Orleans’ jazz districts, Medellín’s street art scene, and the historic neighborhoods of Savannah, while they dream of a pilgrimage to Ghana’s coastal heritage sites once their ministry fund stabilizes.
info.culinary_persona: Lacedrick Williams cooks energetic soul‑food dishes like collard greens seasoned with smoked turkey, sweet‑potato pie spiced with cinnamon, and okra‑gumbo, experimenting in the community garden to fuse traditional flavors with fresh produce, though they often improvise recipes late at night after rehearsals.

info.persona: Jenny Santiago’s blend of competitive spark, relaxed scheduling, bilingual charisma, and a kitchen that constantly experiments with Spanish‑Southern flavors defines a lively, adaptable spirit who thrives on turning spontaneous ideas into shared experiences.
info.professional_persona: A community‑focused culinary entrepreneur, Jenny Santiago blends bilingual fluency, budget‑savvy event coordination, and a love for Spanish‑Southern fusion to launch a home‑based catering business while eyeing a part‑time role with the Columbia Chamber of Commerce.
info.cultural_background: Jenny is a first‑generation American of Spanish descent. She grew up in a bilingual household where traditional Spanish holidays—such as Semana Santa and Día de los Reyes—were celebrated alongside Southern customs like barbecues and church picnics. Her family’s emphasis on hospitality and shared meals fuels her love for cooking and community gatherings. While she embraces her Spanish heritage through language, music, and cuisine, she also identifies with the close‑knit, neighborly spirit of Williamson County, often blending the two cultures in her daily life.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Jenny loves activities that combine movement, creativity, and social interaction. She regularly attends salsa and flamenco dance classes, experiments with Spanish and Southern dishes in her kitchen, and participates in group fitness sessions like Zumba and boot‑camp. On weekends she hikes the Natchez Trace and local parks, volunteers at the community food pantry, hosts game nights for friends, and enjoys DIY home projects and reading mystery novels for relaxation.
info.sports_persona: An avid participant in salsa, Zumba, and boot‑camp sessions, Jenny Santiago also hikes the Natchez Trace regularly, cheers for the Columbia Fireflies baseball team, and belongs to the Midtown Trailblazers running club for weekend group runs.
info.arts_persona: Creative and socially inclined, Jenny Santiago refines her artistic side through weekly salsa and flamenco lessons set to the rhythms of Celia Cruz and Alvaro Soler, devours mystery novels by Agatha Christie and Gillian Flynn, and curates photo‑video highlights for local events, while occasionally attending productions at the Columbia Performing Arts Center.
info.travel_persona: With a penchant for spontaneous weekend getaways, Jenny Santiago has explored the Natchez Trace, taken a culinary pilgrimage to Sevilla’s tapas bars, plans a future trip to New Orleans for gumbo inspiration, and balances wanderlust with a modest travel budget and a flexible work schedule.
info.culinary_persona: An inventive home chef, Jenny Santiago masterfully fuses Spanish paella with Southern collard greens and smoked pork, crafts jambalaya infused with chorizo and saffron, and delights in perfecting dishes like patatas bravas with pecan praline, showcasing a skillful command of ingredients such as smoked paprika, okra, and fresh cilantro.
